messages:
Ravi: Circling back on onboarding pipeline decisions. I want to propose a small, deterministic 'admit' score output from the bench/validator that the controller can consume instead of lots of bespoke checks. Thoughts?
Lina: Curious what fields you want in the score. A single float is easy but we lose signal about why it failed.
Ravi: Agreed. Plan: admit_score (0-100) + vector of tags explaining failures (latency_p95, mem_headroom, tokenizer_mismatch, golden_divergence). Keep tags optional and bounded to 6 entries.
Omar: We already compute p95/p99 and tokenization diffs in bench. Adding admit_score as a derived scalar should be cheap. How to map score->action?
Priya: Controller policy: score >=80 => auto-accept canary; 60-79 => require human signoff; <60 => reject. These thresholds are tunable via config.
QA-Jen: Tests: ensure borderline cases (score 79->manual) are plumbed to the UI with clear rationales. Also require that tags include the top-3 contributing signals.
Lina: For benchmarks, we need normalized scales. Latency is ms, memory is GB, divergence is KL or BLEU. How do we fold to 0-100 consistently?
Ravi: Use per-metric scoring functions defined in model metadata; default set in platform: latency (target_p95_ms) maps linearly to score contribution, mem_headroom maps to safety margin, accuracy/divergence scaled by eval-specific thresholds. Model owners can override.
Omar: Don't forget cost: if model token cost >> baseline, that should deduct points. We can include cost_delta tag.
Priya: Good call. Also want a 'canary_window' policy: even with score >=80, we still run a 10-minute canary with synthetic traffic and live shadowing traffic to watch for unseen regressions.
Lina: How do we surface tokenization mismatches? Those can be subtle: differing vocab can change decoding. Suggest a tokenizer_compat boolean and an example mismatch snippet in badge data.
QA-Jen: For golden artifacts: bench should attempt a small golden set replay during preflight. If golden divergence > threshold, put 'golden_divergence' tag with sample ids that failed. But this is expensive for very large models; make golden replay optional and gated by model metadata (golden_required: true/false).
Ravi: Agree. Default golden_required=false for >10B models. Owners can opt-in. Also include a 'golden_sample_seed' used for deterministic picks.
Omar: Multi-shard models: bench should emit per-shard mem_headroom and worst_shard_id; admit_score should incorporate worst_shard normalization to avoid masking a bad shard.
Priya: For compatibility checks: we need explicit compatibility tags in model manifest: {streaming: true, kv_store: v2, quantized_safe: false}. Controller uses these tags to select fallback variants.
Lina: On fallbacks: controller should prefer quantized fallback only if quantized_safe=true in manifest. Otherwise pick a smaller model with compatible tokenizer and kv bindings.
QA-Jen: Telemetry: emit admit_score and top_tags as low-cardinality metrics. Don't emit full tag list at high cardinality to control cost. On failures, emit full event with sample ids to S3 for triage.
Ravi: Rollout plan: introduce admit_score v1 as opt-in per-team. After 4 weeks of stable behavior (low false positive/negative), flip default to enabled for new models. Leave legacy boolean gating for 2 months before deprecation.
Omar: Implementation notes: bench pipeline will produce JSON artifact: admit.json containing {admit_score:int, top_tags:[str], metric_breakdown:optional_b64}. Make artifact small. Controller pulls artifact from artifact-store.
Priya: Controller actions mapping: accept -> start canary with 1% traffic, watch admit_monitoring signals for 10m, then ramp. manual -> create PR and notify model-owner; reject -> stop intake and generate rollback playbook.
QA-Jen: Add e2e tests that fuzz metric contributions to ensure scoring is stable and not overly sensitive to tiny runtime noise (e.g., p95 jitter of 5ms shouldn't flip 20 points).
Lina: Concern: this central score becomes a bottleneck for trust. Need clear docs + open source scoring helpers so owners can inspect the function.
Ravi: Absolutely. We'll add scoring library in devex with reference implementations and a visualizer in Console showing how each metric contributed to final score.
ops-bot: note: will add alerting rule: if admit_score drops >30 points between consecutive benches -> create incident in #eng-ml and page model-owner.
Priya: Last bit: compatibility checks timeline. Bench runs (fast smoke), then full validation (longer) if admit_score>=60. If full validation fails, we downgrade admit_score by 30 and mark manual.
Ravi: OK I'll open a follow-up PR with schema, default scoring functions, and rollout plan. Thanks all. :rocket:
